risks.message: 4 SQL statements executed on every iteration of this LOOP (lines 38, 60, 62, 65): one database round-trip each per row. Prefer set-based statements.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Collapse per-row statements inside loops into one set-based statement.

architectural_decisions.decision: Rewrote the cursor loop (fee lookup, balance update, transaction insert, audit insert per row) as a single set-based CTE statement with LATERAL join for the fee lookup.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Rule 7: semantics allow it; the per-row statements are independent (no row locks, no procedural branching beyond the fee lookup and the CASE multiplier), so one statement preserves behaviour while removing 4 round-trips per row.

architectural_decisions.decision: The UPDATE contas uses a source subquery aggregated by conta_origem_id (SUM of taxa) instead of joining the per-row rows directly.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Rule 13: UPDATE ... FROM applies at most one source row per target; several transactions of the same account must accumulate on saldo, matching the original sequential per-row updates.

architectural_decisions.decision: Reproduced each PL/pgSQL assignment rounding with CAST(... AS NUMERIC(18,2)) at the exact same points: after GREATEST(valor*percentual/100.0, minimo) and again after the 1.10/0.90 multiplier.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Rule 12: a single combined expression would round only once and change results; the original rounds v_taxa on every assignment.

architectural_decisions.decision: No commit/rollback in the module; both statements run on the caller's connection/transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The original procedure does not manage transactions; the caller owns them.

architectural_decisions.decision: The trailing SELECT of the CTE statement returns COUNT(*) and SUM(taxa), which are passed as typed bind parameters (CAST AS INT / NUMERIC(18,2)) to the final log_auditoria insert.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Keeps the totals computation in SQL (relational aggregate) while the final insert stays a separate parameterized statement; CASTs satisfy asyncpg's polymorphic-parameter inference (rule 10).

warnings: The original cursor had no ORDER BY, so per-row processing order was unspecified; the set-based rewrite is order-independent and produces the same final state (saldo updates accumulate via SUM, inserts are unordered).
The inserted TARIFA transactions get data_transacao = NOW() (default), exactly as in the original; they are excluded from reprocessing by the tipo <> 'TARIFA' filter.
Rows whose transaction type has no matching fee row (percentual IS NULL) are skipped, as in the original CONTINUE; the LEFT JOIN LATERAL reproduces this.
jsonb_build_object values are column references (typed by the schema), so only the bind parameters of the final log insert required explicit CASTs.
If a conta_origem_id no longer exists (dangling FK impossible per schema, but defensive note), the UPDATE silently skips it, same as the original UPDATE ... WHERE id = v_origem.
